ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.method: A STRUCTURAL sweep over every tracked blob in the target tree (git ls-tree -r), distinguishing an ALLOCATION POSITION from a mere literal occurrence. An allocation position is a parsed-JSON member whose KEY is one of GRANT_ID, authorityId, grant_id, authority_id, controller_id, node_id, artifact_id, version, branch, action or protected_authority and whose VALUE matches the candidate EXACTLY - never a substring in prose, never a bare array element. A FIXED-STRING containment sweep over raw bytes was run alongside it, and every literal hit was classified by reading its containing clause.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_the_two_sweeps_are_both_needed: A value-exact sweep that ignored key position would count prohibition-list array elements as allocations. A key-position sweep alone would report ZERO and prove nothing about whether the id is discussed elsewhere. Reporting both, and classifying every literal, is what makes the negative non-vacuous.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_FIXED_STRING_and_not_regex: git grep treats '.' as a wildcard, so a regex search for 1.0.32 matches the substring 1/0032 inside the text 0031/0032 and manufactures a phantom hit in docs/ops/security/PLATFORM_ADMIN_RLS_SUPERADMIN_POLICY_CENSUS_v1.0.0.json. git grep -F on that same file returns ZERO. The sweep below uses fixed-string containment and is unaffected. The false positive is disclosed rather than filtered, because an auditor re-running the naive form will reproduce it and must be able to see it was classified.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.limitation_disclosed: The structural walker parses JSON only. scripts/ods-scope.ts and scripts/ods-controller.ts are TypeScript, so their PROTECTED_GRANTS rows and IMMUTABLE_BY_CONVENTION entries were enumerated SEPARATELY, by extracting each array literal via structural bracket matching, evaluating it, asserting a non-zero length, and reading each element. Those enumerations are grant_state.registered_ids_in_array_order and controller_state.composition_measured above, and they are what establishes that no PROTECTED_GRANTS row carries HPO-ODS-W2-29 and no IMMUTABLE_BY_CONVENTION entry names v1.0.32.
ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP.why_the_denominators_are_stated: A checker that reports zero says nothing until it says how much it examined. 765 allocation positions were evaluated across 114021 parsed JSON objects in 305 JSON files out of 1994 tracked blobs; the zero is a measurement over that population, not an absence of measurement.

protected_grant.ORDER_IS_BINDING: The three patterns are stated in the order above and MUST be registered in that order. Order is part of the row identity, because the registration control asserts the row by whole-object equality and not by set comparison.
protected_grant.BRANCH_BINDING_IS_EXACT: The bound branch is the exact string codex/l1-organization-commercial-acceptance-implementation-r1. Resolution is by exact string equality, never by prefix, pattern or family. This branch does not exist at START_HEAD - measured across all local and remote refs - which is correct and expected: the grant is declared before the implementation branch is cut.
protected_grant.BRANCH_NAME_IS_AN_IMPLEMENTATION_CHOICE_: Neither the Customer Lifecycle parent authority nor the companion L1 execution authority inherits a FUTURE_IMPLEMENTATION_BRANCH key from a grandparent. The branch name is therefore CHOSEN by this allocation, in the shape the three most recent implementation lanes use (codex/commercial-account-ce1-implementation-r1, codex/fibdb052-p1-implementation-r1, codex/customer-lifecycle-cl1-implementation-r1). It is binding from the moment this artifact is integrated.
protected_grant.STOP_FOR_GRANT_BRANCH_MISMATCH: If the L1 implementation is ever attempted from a branch whose name is not byte-identical to the bound branch, the grant contributes zero patterns, the protected write is refused, and the mission STOPS. A gate that refuses is the control working, not an obstacle to route around. Renaming the branch to match, or rebinding the grant to whichever branch happens to exist, are both PROHIBITED without a governed successor.

WHY_THESE_THREE_PATTERNS_RE_DERIVED_NOT_.method: git diff --numstat cbd1eb82^1 cbd1eb82, which emits one row per changed path with SEPARATE insertion and deletion columns and FULL unabbreviated paths. --stat is unsafe as a measurement input and unsafe in a way that fails silently: it abbreviates long paths, so a grep on a directory prefix under-counts, and its single column is insertions PLUS deletions, so a one-line rewrite reads as 2.

PATTERN_1_db_migrations.why_the_glob_and_not_literals: A migration is never one file: the generate path emits the SQL, a per-ordinal snapshot, and an append to _journal.json. L1 creates one new relation with RLS and two triggers, so it will produce at least one SQL file, at least one snapshot and a journal append - and it may produce two migrations, as CL-1 in fact did. The ordinal is not knowable in advance (posture B), so a literal-path grant is not constructible. db/migrations/** is a member of DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS (scripts/ods-scope.ts:82), so the grant is required.

PATTERN_2_db_prepared_journal.measured: EIGHTY-FOUR paths under db/prepared/journal/ changed in the CL-1 merge, in exactly TWO numstat buckets: 82 paths at (1 insertion, 1 deletion) and 2 paths at (65 insertions, 0 deletions).
PATTERN_2_db_prepared_journal.the_mechanism: Each wrapper header carries the literal Unit <ordinal>/<BASELINE_UNITS.length>, stamped by db/hosted/baseline-journal-wrapper.ts. Appending a baseline unit increments the DENOMINATOR, which rewrites that ONE header line in EVERY pre-existing wrapper. The two (65,0) rows are the two NEW wrappers CL-1 added (083 and 084). This is a GENERATED-ARTIFACT REGENERATION, not an edit of unrelated files.
PATTERN_2_db_prepared_journal.why_the_glob_is_the_MINIMUM_and_not_a_co: A grant naming only the new wrapper path would refuse EIGHTY-TWO regenerated siblings and the mission would STOP on a scope violation it cannot lawfully route around. Enumerating 84 literal paths that will be 85 next time is not a grant, it is a stale list. The glob is the only constructible pattern.
PATTERN_2_db_prepared_journal.independently_confirmed_by_the_OTHER_pre: The same two-bucket distribution was measured by v1.0.31 for both the CE-1 commit (80 at (1,1) plus 1 at (65,0)) and the P1 commit (81 at (1,1) plus 1 at (65,0)). The count grows by one per landed migration, exactly as the mechanism predicts, which is itself evidence the mechanism is understood rather than merely observed.
PATTERN_2_db_prepared_journal.removing_it: Eighty-two regenerated wrappers are refused. db/prepared/** is a member of DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS, so the grant is required.

PATTERN_3_db_prepared_checkpoint_b0_obse.the_rule_it_must_satisfy: W2-27 DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED this literal, under a rule permitting inclusion ONLY IF a live re-measurement proves the mission actually changes the file. That rule is applied here rather than assumed away.
PATTERN_3_db_prepared_checkpoint_b0_obse.measured: db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql changed in the CL-1 merge with numstat (6 insertions, 0 deletions) - CL-1 created THREE relations and each added two lines to the chain.
PATTERN_3_db_prepared_checkpoint_b0_obse.the_mechanism_verified_in_the_file_itsel: observation.sql builds its rowCounts key from an explicit UNION ALL chain with one arm per governed relation. The three CL-1 relations are now arms in that chain, at lines 91 (public.account_legal_acceptances), 127 (public.legal_instrument_versions) and 129 (public.legal_instruments). Adding an arm changes the FILE BYTES, not merely the query output.
PATTERN_3_db_prepared_checkpoint_b0_obse.therefore_for_L1: L1 creates ONE new governed relation, so it adds ONE arm and the file bytes change. L1 falls on the SAME side of the discriminator as CL-1 and the OPPOSITE side from P1.
PATTERN_3_db_prepared_checkpoint_b0_obse.the_discriminator_validated_in_BOTH_dire: TABLE-creating commits move the file (CE-1: 1 table, observation.sql (2,0); CL-1: 3 relations, observation.sql (6,0) - and the line count scales with the relation count, which is the mechanism showing itself). INDEX-only commits do not (P1: 0 tables, the path does not appear in the commit at all). The two axes are INDEPENDENT: journal-wrapper regeneration happens for ALL of them because all append a baseline unit, so pattern 2 is required regardless of what the migration contains, while pattern 3 is what distinguishes a relation-creating mission from an index-only one.

PATTERN_3_db_prepared_checkpoint_b0_obse.a_LITERAL_and_not_a_glob: The pattern is the single literal path, never db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/**. Only this one file needs to move.

protected_grant.NO_DB_PREPARED_WIDENING: BINDING. The prepared-surface patterns are the narrow db/prepared/journal/** and the single literal db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql - NEVER a blanket db/prepared/**. The DEFAULT protected pattern in scripts/ods-scope.ts IS the broad db/prepared/**, and the breadth of the PROTECTION is not a licence for breadth in the GRANT. A blanket grant would additionally authorize db/prepared/hosted/** and db/prepared/hosted/governed/**, which are G2-gated apply surfaces L1 has no business touching, and db/prepared/stella_*.sql, a separate numbering family L1 does not extend. A sibling under db/prepared/ that matches the default pattern but not these narrower patterns is CORRECTLY refused.
protected_grant.why_the_unprotected_entries_are_listed_a: db/policies/**, the two scripts and the two ODS test files are NOT members of DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS and therefore need no grant to be written. They are named in the prohibition list so that no reader infers from their absence that the grant was silently understood to cover them. Naming a path in a prohibition is never an allocation and never a grant. db/policies/** in particular is named because the L1 RLS work could plausibly be mistaken for belonging there: it does NOT. The measured precedent for an acceptance-relation policy is a MIGRATION - 0070 - not a db/policies unit. scripts/ods-scope.ts is named because it is where the W2-29 REGISTRATION act will land, and that act is explicitly not authorized here. The two sealed authority artifacts are named because this mission is their successor and a successor editing its parent is the specific failure fail-closed exists to prevent.
protected_grant.grant_does_not_replace_allow: The grant widens what the bound branch MAY write; it does not populate the mission's --allow list. The implementing mission must still derive its own --allow list from its own measured diff at its own base, and a protected path in that diff which this grant does not cover is a SCOPE DELTA requiring adjudication - never a silent addition on the ground that it changed anyway.

UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_L1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.status: INFORMATIVE, NOT A GRANT. Every path below is OUTSIDE DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS and needs an --allow entry, never a grant. Listing them prevents the implementing mission from reading the grant as the whole of its write surface.
UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_L1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.measured_basis: The CL-1 merge touched 131 paths in total, of which 90 were protected (5 migrations, 84 journal wrappers, 1 observation script) and 41 were unprotected - db/schema.ts, db/hosted/baseline-manifest.ts, the two lib/auth modules, lib/audit/logger.ts, app routes and actions, tests and workflows among them.
UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_L1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.lib_audit_logger_carries_an_ADDITIONAL_o: It is unprotected in the ODS sense and therefore needs only an --allow entry, but it is held by LOCK-AUDIT-ACTION-VOCABULARY. Absence from DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS is not absence of a lock, and an implementer who reads the ODS classification as the whole picture would write it without resolving the lock.
UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_L1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.a_dedicated_real_PG_workflow_is_REQUIRED: .github/workflows/** is unprotected, and the companion test manifest requires a dedicated non-vacuous real-PostgreSQL workflow with an explicit PG environment flag, an explicit *_PG_REQUIRED anti-skip self-check, and no --passWithNoTests.
UNPROTECTED_SURFACES_L1_WILL_ALSO_TOUCH.NOT_AN_AUTHORIZATION: This list authorizes none of these paths. It records which of them are unprotected so that the implementing mission derives an --allow list rather than assuming the grant covers everything it needs.

protected_grant.why_existing_grants_cannot_be_reused: MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. Eight registered grants carry the db/migrations/** or db/prepared/journal/** families - W2-01, W2-12, W2-17, W2-20 with W2-21, W2-25, W2-26, W2-27 and W2-28 - and five carry db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql: W2-07, W2-16, W2-17, W2-26 and W2-28. Every one of them is bound to a DIFFERENT branch. Resolution is by exact branch equality, so on codex/l1-organization-commercial-acceptance-implementation-r1 all of them contribute ZERO patterns. In particular W2-28, whose three patterns are byte-identical to this row's, is bound to codex/customer-lifecycle-cl1-implementation-r1 and resolves nowhere for L1. A new row is therefore doing real work and is not a duplicate.

MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.POSTURE: B - NO ORDINAL IS ALLOCATED. Permission is granted for the implementing lane to derive the ordinal at its own exact implementation HEAD, by the normal drizzle-kit generate path.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.why_posture_B_and_not_A: This is not a choice made by this lane; it is the pattern ODS authority has established and the only one the record supports. v1.0.30 and v1.0.31 both set allocated, reserved and implied to false, recorded the first free candidate as a DATED OBSERVATION, and imposed a re-measurement obligation in exactly these terms. The Customer Lifecycle parent independently requires the same thing from the other direction: LINEAGE_REDERIVATION_REQUIRED is YES, scope EVERY object without exception.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.candidate_derivation: The highest existing db/migrations/NNNN_*.sql ordinal at START_HEAD is 0071_customer_lifecycle_cl1_content_bytes.sql, and db/migrations/meta/_journal.json holds max idx 71 across 72 entries. 0072 is therefore the first free candidate AT THIS HEAD.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.THIS_IS_NOT_A_RESERVATION: BINDING. 0072 is recorded as a DATED OBSERVATION and nothing more. It is not allocated, not reserved, and confers no entitlement. Concurrent lanes may land a migration between this artifact and the implementing mission.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.THE_WINDOW_IS_DEMONSTRATED_AND_NOT_MEREL: v1.0.31 recorded 0070 as its first free candidate off a tail of 0069. The CL-1 implementation then landed TWO migrations, 0070 AND 0071. A lane that had treated v1.0.31's observation as a reservation would have been wrong, and wrong by two rather than by one. This is no longer a theoretical hazard in this lineage: it has already happened once, at the immediately preceding ordinal.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.re_measurement_obligation: The migration ordinal MUST be re-measured by the implementing mission at its OWN live head and produced by the normal drizzle-kit generate path. It is not computed by this artifact.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.uniqueness_proof_not_required_because_no: A uniqueness proof against both migrations and prepared migrations is required IF a specific ordinal is allocated. None is. The proof obligation therefore does not arise, and manufacturing one here would imply an allocation this artifact does not make.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.prepared_family_note: The db/prepared/ root carries a SEPARATE numbering family (stella_NNNN and stella_hosted_NNNN) whose tail at START_HEAD is stella_hosted_0008 and stella_0020. L1 does NOT extend that family. The prepared artifact L1 will add is a db/prepared/journal/ wrapper, whose index derives from the baseline unit count (84 at this head), not from the migration ordinal.
MIGRATION_ORDINAL_DISPOSITION.ONE_HEAVY_POSTGRESQL_JOB_AT_A_TIME: PRESERVED AND BINDING. The L1 implementation requires a real-PostgreSQL disposable-harness probe, which is not safely concurrent. L1 must hold REAL_POSTGRESQL_EXCLUSIVE, and must not hold LOCK_MIGRATION_WRITER concurrently with any other lane that writes db/migrations. Several sibling authorities are live and each has DISCLAIMED the next ordinal rather than taken it, which is precisely the situation in which two lanes can both believe the tail is free. A separate, measured hazard applies to CI: dispatching several real-PostgreSQL gates in a burst throttles the container registry, and a throttled run can present as a skip rather than as a failure - which is why the companion manifest requires an explicit anti-skip self-check.

NO_NODE_ID_IS_ALLOCATED_BECAUSE_NO_SUCH_.measured: The canonical allocation axes are exactly three: the addendum version (docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.<N>.json), the protected grant id (HPO-ODS-W2-<N>, registered in scripts/ods-scope.ts PROTECTED_GRANTS), and the Controller ordinal (the IMMUTABLE_BY_CONVENTION array length in scripts/ods-controller.ts). docs/ops/ods/ODS_PROGRAM_STATE_REGISTRY_v1.0.0.json carries units keyed W2-B1 through W2-B5 and its own purpose field states that it is operational metadata, NOT new authority, and that adding or extending a unit entry there is ordinary tooling maintenance rather than an authority act. It is therefore not an allocator, and an L1 entry in it would allocate nothing.

MINIMALITY.claim: This is the minimum allocation that lets the bounded L1 implementation proceed, and no more.
MINIMALITY.one_lineage_ordinal: v1.0.32. A successor WITHIN the CL-1 lineage was considered and REJECTED: v1.0.25 through v1.0.27 each reused HPO-ODS-W2-25 and v1.0.28 with v1.0.29 reused W2-26, because each group comprises successors of ONE mission. L1 is a genuinely new mission lineage - a different bounded object, a different execution authority, a different branch and a different accepting principal - so it takes a new ordinal and a new grant.
MINIMALITY.one_grant: HPO-ODS-W2-29. A second grant was considered and REJECTED: the three patterns are all reachable from one branch in one mission, and W2-20 with W2-21 splitting db/migrations/** from db/prepared/journal/** across two rows is a historical artifact of that lane, not a rule.
MINIMALITY.three_patterns: Each is re-derived from the measured CL-1 merge diff at THIS head, not copied from W2-28. Removing any one causes a demonstrable scope refusal on the L1 diff shape; a fourth was not justified by any measurement, and db/baseline/** was checked and found not to move.
MINIMALITY.no_controller_allocation: The next Controller act is a separate governed act and is not performed, labelled or numbered here.
MINIMALITY.no_migration_ordinal: Posture B, per established precedent, and with the window demonstrated by a real over-run at the immediately preceding ordinal.
MINIMALITY.no_audit_vocabulary_write: The verb LITERAL is allocated by the companion execution authority. The WRITE to lib/audit/logger.ts is not authorized, and the lock that holds it is neither acquired nor released.
MINIMALITY.no_runtime_and_no_sql: This artifact and its two companions are docs-only. No migration SQL, no schema edit, no runtime edit, no test edit, no workflow edit, no hosted mutation, no PostgreSQL execution.

protected_grants_count_rule: This artifact DECLARES the grant and does not REGISTER it. scripts/ods-scope.ts is not edited here and the row count is unchanged at 16. A future governed registration act adds the row, taking the count to 17 and requiring the corresponding updates to tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts, which at START_HEAD pins the registry against W2-29's ABSENCE at :412-417, :1250-1260, :1626, :1637-1641 and :1795, and which asserts at :1641 that HPO-ODS-W2-29 has ZERO textual occurrences in scripts/ods-scope.ts. That registration is NOT authorized by this artifact.

GRANT_REGISTRATION_IS_A_SEPARATE_GOVERNE.binding: Registration of HPO-ODS-W2-29 in scripts/ods-scope.ts is a SEPARATE governed act, performed after this authority package is independently certified and integrated.
GRANT_REGISTRATION_IS_A_SEPARATE_GOVERNE.THE_IMPLEMENTATION_WRITER_MAY_NOT_SELF_R: The L1 implementation mission MAY NOT register its own grant. A mission that could grant itself a protected surface has no protected surface, and the separation is the only thing that makes the gate meaningful.
GRANT_REGISTRATION_IS_A_SEPARATE_GOVERNE.THE_REGISTRATION_ACT_CARRIES_ITS_OWN_MEA: Registering a grant requires an ATOMIC transfer of the live-count guard: a demote-without-promote leaves ZERO guards and the suite passes VACUOUSLY. The registering act must promote the new absence literal in the same change that demotes the old one, and must verify the guard count is non-zero at every intermediate state rather than only at the end.
GRANT_REGISTRATION_IS_A_SEPARATE_GOVERNE.why_stated_here: So the registering mission does not discover it, and so an auditor can check that the registration was atomic rather than merely correct at its endpoint.

when_L1_becomes_implementation_authorize: L1 becomes implementation-authorized only AFTER ALL THREE of: (a) the companion execution authority package passes INDEPENDENT CERTIFICATION and is integrated; (b) the HPO-ODS-W2-29 registration is INTEGRATED - that is, a PROTECTED_GRANTS row with authorityId HPO-ODS-W2-29 and branch codex/l1-organization-commercial-acceptance-implementation-r1 resolves at the implementing mission's own head; and (c) the implementing mission re-derives its migration ordinal, its known_conditions and every line anchor in the execution authority's ATTACHMENT_TOPOLOGY at its own live head. Integration of THIS artifact confers none of the three. Neither does the existence of the companion execution authority, whose own IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED_NOTE states the same thing in its own words.

KTC_RULE.binding: This artifact FREEZES NO known_conditions set for L1. The companion test manifest declares known_conditions as an EXPLICIT EMPTY ARRAY for the pre-implementation commitment, and the implementing mission MUST RE-DERIVE its own set at its OWN exact HEAD.
KTC_RULE.why_the_empty_array_is_a_commitment_and_: An explicit empty array states that no waiver is claimed. It is not a frozen assertion that none will ever apply. scripts/ods-test-diff.ts matches a known condition on test identity plus a comparable failure signature - test_file, test_id and the failure's leading line - and NOT on cause_fingerprint, so a condition frozen against a stale HEAD could silently absorb a real L1 failure under byte-identical identity. Omitting the key entirely would let a validator treat it as satisfied; declaring it empty makes the claim explicit and falsifiable.

risks_and_open_findings.finding: Another lane may consume ODS ordinal v1.0.32, grant HPO-ODS-W2-29, the bound branch name, or the audit literal legal.organization_instrument_accepted between this artifact and its integration.
risks_and_open_findings.measured_basis: Several sibling authorities are live and each names a next-ordinal candidate inside an explicit non-allocation clause. Their disclaimers are evidence that the window is RECOGNISED, not that it is CLOSED - and the migration axis has already over-run once in this lineage, at 0070/0071.
risks_and_open_findings.mitigation: The collision sweep is specified by method and is re-runnable. An auditor or a successor MUST re-run it at the merge base rather than trusting this record.

risks_and_open_findings.finding: Two literal-search hazards were hit and corrected during this lane's own measurement. Both fail SILENTLY, which is why they are recorded rather than merely avoided.
items: A TypeScript array literal declared as `export const X: string[] = [` defeats an extractor that searches for the first '[' after the '=' sign, because the type annotation `string[]` contains one. The extractor returned a ZERO-LENGTH array and no error, so DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS initially measured as 0 patterns. The fix is to anchor on the FULL declaration including its type annotation, and to ASSERT a non-zero length before using the result. A structural extraction that silently yields nothing is more dangerous than one that throws, because a zero-length protected-pattern list makes every path look unprotected.

git grep treats '.' as a regex wildcard, so a search for 1.0.32 matches the substring 1/0032 inside the prose text 0031/0032 and produced a phantom hit in docs/ops/security/PLATFORM_ADMIN_RLS_SUPERADMIN_POLICY_CENSUS_v1.0.0.json. git grep -F returns ZERO on the same file. The sweep reported in ALLOCATION_COLLISION_SWEEP uses fixed-string containment and is unaffected; the false positive is disclosed there so an auditor re-running the naive form can see it was classified rather than missed.
risks_and_open_findings.what_survived_unchanged: Every allocation identity, every count and every pattern derivation. Both defects were caught before any figure entered this artifact, and both were caught by the same discipline: a negative or a length must be cross-checked by a second method before it is reported.

risks_and_open_findings.finding: db/migrations/0042_fib_audit_insert_policy.sql's audit_logs_insert_member_or_admin carries an OR current_user_is_super_admin() disjunct and constrains no action string, so a super-admin could write an L1 acceptance AUDIT row for an acceptance they cannot themselves perform.
risks_and_open_findings.consequence: The audit row ALONE is not proof of a valid acceptance. The acceptance relation is the record. An auditor reconstructing acceptances must read it, not audit_logs.
risks_and_open_findings.disposition: REPORTED, NOT REPAIRED, AND NOT IN SCOPE. Narrowing 0042 is outside this authority and is adjacent to U-AO-8. Recorded so a successor does not read L1's silence as a claim that the audit trail is self-certifying.

risks_and_open_findings.finding: U-AO-8 remains OPEN and was re-verified at this head: db/migrations/0031_rls_core.sql:126-134 members_insert_admin carries an OR current_user_is_super_admin() disjunct and no later migration narrows it, so a platform principal can self-assign an organization_admin membership and would then pass L1's exact-equality predicate legitimately.
risks_and_open_findings.disposition: OUT OF SCOPE, NOT REPAIRED, RECORDED SO THE GUARANTEE IS NOT OVERSTATED. Non-blocking for L1 implementation; a promotion consideration for the platform-admin lineage. RAT-OP-01 independently treats the closure of this path as an unmet prerequisite.

risks_and_open_findings.finding: HPO-ODS-W2-29 is DECLARED here and NOT REGISTERED. L1 cannot lawfully write a protected path until a separate governed act adds the row to scripts/ods-scope.ts and atomically transfers the live-count guard in tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts.
risks_and_open_findings.why_this_is_by_design: Allocation and registration are separate governed acts throughout this lineage. v1.0.30 declared W2-27 as DECLARED_NOT_REGISTERED and v1.0.31 declared W2-28 the same way; both registrations landed in later missions.

risks_and_open_findings.finding: Dispatching several real-PostgreSQL gates in a burst throttles the container registry, and a throttled run can present as a SKIP rather than as a failure - the harness setupStatus value SKIPPED is also its initialization value, so a run that never reached setup is indistinguishable from one that deliberately skipped.
risks_and_open_findings.consequence_for_L1: A skipped real-PG suite would otherwise read as green, which for a unit whose entire security argument lives at the database boundary is the worst possible failure mode.
risks_and_open_findings.mitigation_carried_into_the_manifest: An explicit *_PG_REQUIRED anti-skip self-check that FAILS on a skip, an explicit PG environment flag, a prohibition on --passWithNoTests, and the ONE_HEAVY_POSTGRESQL_JOB_AT_A_TIME requirement above.
